name: body-parser-req-body-no-longer-initialized-body-parser-xml
behavioral_change: In body-parser v_old (1.20.2) every parser middleware executed `req.body = req.body || {}` before deciding whether to read the request body, so `req.body` was always an object even when parsing was skipped. From v_new (2.0.0) this default initialisation was removed; in 2.3.0 lib/read.js sets `req.body = undefined` when absent and calls `next()` directly when there is no body or the type does not match, leaving `req.body` undefined.
downstream_effect: body-parser-xml's index.js runs `bodyParser.text(options)` first and passes the request on when `typeof req.body !== 'string'`; after the upgrade `req.body` is `undefined` instead of `{}` on that path, JSON serialisation drops the key, and the test fails with `expected { parsed: {} } response body, got {}`. The stack frame points only at test.js:112 and supertest internals; nothing in the output mentions index.js, req.body, undefined, or the body-parser library.
reference_fix: The reference fix adds one line to index.js, restoring `req.body = req.body || {}` in the pass-through branch before `return next()`.
documented_in: body-parser's HISTORY.md at https://github.com/expressjs/body-parser/blob/v2.3.0/HISTORY.md, 2.0.0 Breaking Changes, states that `req.body` is no longer always initialized to `{}` and is left `undefined` unless a body is parsed. The documentation gives only prose and no adaptation code; the reference fix's form is taken from body-parser 1.20.2's own lib/types/text.js, not from any official guidance.
failing_tests: test.js :: XML Body Parser › should ignore non-XML
